assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new platform in which flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity are tunable in one device. It is a clear case of experiment overturning expectation and of quantum mechanics offering a new surprise in materials. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted the magic angle quantitatively before the 2018 experiments, which is the theory-to-experiment link I value most.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction of the flat-band condition; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 observations of correlated insulating and superconducting states. This forms a natural theory-plus-experiment prize. Experimental co-discoverers and early twisted-bilayer theorists outside the credited list could complicate the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Dozens of independent groups have reproduced the correlated phases, and the field is large and still growing. Recognition is timely; the mechanism of the superconductivity remains debated, but the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism in the superconducting phase is unresolved.
Sample-to-sample variability and twist-angle disorder complicate reproducibility details.
Credit to other early contributors outside the supplied names is not captured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators revealed a new class of quantum matter with protected edge or surface states, with a transparent link to band-structure theory and spectroscopy. The concept has had broad impact across condensed matter and spintronics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the foundational theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group observed quantum spin Hall edge transport in HgTe following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal (not on the supplied list). Hasan did key 3D topological insulator ARPES work. A three-person prize with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is plausible, but the allocation between 2D and 3D work and between theory and experiment is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many groups in several materials, with ARPES and transport agreement; the interpretation is stable and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Compound discovery: 2D quantum spin Hall versus 3D topological insulators may need different credit.
Omission of Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and others from the supplied credit may be unfair; I cannot verify that independently.
B003 and B040 overlap in subject; I prefer this entry for its broader credited set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is the standard quantitative framework for strongly correlated electrons, combining with DFT (DFT+DMFT) to treat the Mott transition and correlated materials. It is a theory contribution directly relevant to my own field and to interpreting measured spectra.
assessment.attribution: Georges and Kotliar developed the mapping onto an impurity model and the DMFT framework; Vollhardt, with Metzner, established the infinite-dimension limit (Metzner is not in the supplied credit, so the attribution is incomplete). Credit for the original limit versus the method is a real allocation issue.
assessment.maturity: Over three decades of use, validated against many experiments and numerical benchmarks; mature. Limits in cluster and non-local extensions remain.
uncertainties: Walter Metzner and Erwin Muller-Hartmann were central to the infinite-dimension limit and are absent from the credit.
Committees may judge a method prize as less of a discrete physical discovery.
Quantitative predictive power for real materials varies.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: ARPES turned a spectroscopic probe into a direct measurement of electronic band structure, Fermi surfaces, gaps and many-body self-energies in quantum materials, notably cuprates. It is deeply linked to the calculation-versus-spectra comparison central to my work and to synchrotron facilities.
assessment.attribution: Campuzano and Shen led the application of high-resolution ARPES to cuprate superconductors; Johnson contributed early work. The technique's development involved many groups, including instrument developers and early photoemission pioneers, so credit is diffuse and the claim of a single discovery is weaker.
assessment.maturity: A mature, widely validated technique with decades of independent use. Recognition is timely or even overdue, but it is more a method than a single discovery.
uncertainties: Method-versus-discovery framing may weigh against it.
Diffuse credit among instrument developers and photoemission theorists is not captured by the supplied names.
I leave Johnson out because I am less certain of his decisive role; this is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nd-Fe-B magnets are the strongest permanent magnets and underpin electric motors, wind turbines and data storage, linking the fundamental magnetism of rare-earth intermetallics to sustainable energy technology. The physical underpinnings (4f-3d exchange, anisotropy) are well understood from first-principles theory.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa (sintered, Sumitomo) and Croat (melt-spun, General Motors) discovered the compound independently in 1983-84. This two-person configuration is natural, though priority and the role of related industrial work are historically contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature and enormously impactful, with decades of validation. Recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees it as physics discovery or materials engineering.
Historical priority issues between the two laboratories and industrial involvement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, achieve unprecedented fractional uncertainty and stability and enable tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. The quantitative precision and reproducibility are exemplary.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first demonstrated the lattice clock concept, and Ye developed the highest-performing implementations and the many-body (degenerate Fermi gas) clock. A two-person prize is clean, though Hall and Hansch (2005) overlap with related prior recognition.
assessment.maturity: Independently realized in several laboratories; a redefinition of the second is under discussion, so recognition is timely. This is outside my core expertise, so I defer to AMO colleagues on subtle priority issues.
uncertainties: Jun Ye also appears in another candidate (ultracold molecules), which may matter for configuration.
My knowledge of AMO priority history is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, especially coherent tunneling in MgO, underlies spintronic read heads and MRAM. The spin-dependent tunneling physics is understood with first-principles theory and was experimentally confirmed.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera demonstrated large room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin's group and Yuasa's group demonstrated MgO coherent tunneling in 2004, predicted by theory (Butler, Mathon). The supplied credit omits Yuasa, Butler and Mathon, so allocation is uncertain. Fert and Grunberg were recognized in 2007 for related GMR work.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with independent confirmation and wide technological use. Close to the 2007 prize in subject, which may reduce novelty.
uncertainties: Omitted contributors (Yuasa, Butler, Mathon) weaken the supplied credit.
Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize.
Possible view of this as an engineering extension.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism is a newly identified third class of collinear magnetic order, with spin-split bands at zero net magnetization, relevant to magnetism and spintronics. It is the kind of surprise in magnetism I would like to see recognized once the evidence is firm.
assessment.attribution: Šmejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth developed the classification and symmetry-based theory around 2019-2022; other groups proposed related spin-split antiferromagnets earlier. Allocation versus earlier independent proposals is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Experimental ARPES and other evidence in MnTe and CrSb appeared around 2024. The field is only a few years old and is probably premature for a prize; I would want broader independent confirmation and quantitative DFT-spectra agreement.
uncertainties: Prematurity relative to a typical Nobel timescale.
Priority of earlier related spin-splitting proposals.
Strength and independence of experimental confirmation are still developing; I have not independently verified the latest results.
